abstract: Maintains offshore wave climate models and deployment sea-state projections
system_message:
You are the Marine Weather Forecasting Lead (METL), responsible for maintaining offshore wave climate models, deployment sea-state projections, and upper-air sounding analyses.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains offshore wave climate models and deployment sea-state projections（CLIM）
information_points.content:
METL-CLIM-PRV：For the Cascadia Abyssal Plain Mooring Plan, the modeled sea state deployment window probability of significant wave height remaining below two meters during the target 48-hour vessel positioning and crane deployment window is 94 %.
METL-CLIM-JSR：For the Astoria Fan Deep Trench Array Plan, the modeled sea state deployment window probability of significant wave height remaining below two meters during the target 48-hour vessel positioning and crane deployment window is 82 %.
METL-CLIM-FJ9：For the Hydrate Ridge Seafloor Node Plan, the modeled sea state deployment window probability of significant wave height remaining below two meters during the target 48-hour vessel positioning and crane deployment window is 68 %.

information_points.title: Upper-Air Sounding Analysis（WIND）
information_points.content:
METL-WIND-SN9：For the Astoria Fan Deep Trench Array Plan, NOAA marine boundary layer forecasts indicate a prevailing surface gust speed of 18 knot peak expected surface wind gust velocity over a 60-second gust window at station launch coordinates.
METL-WIND-5GE：For the Cascadia Abyssal Plain Mooring Plan, NOAA marine boundary layer forecasts indicate a prevailing surface gust speed of 24 knot peak expected surface wind gust velocity over a 60-second gust window at station launch coordinates.
METL-WIND-ZYP：For the Hydrate Ridge Seafloor Node Plan, NOAA marine boundary layer forecasts indicate a prevailing surface gust speed of 32 knot peak expected surface wind gust velocity over a 60-second gust window at station launch coordinates.
